items.title: China or the U.S.? Two Meetings Offer Competing Showcases of Global Power.
items.summary: As Xi Jinping gathered with the leaders of Russia and Iran, Europe challenged the Trump administration at the G20, offering a split-screen view of a changing world.

items.title: The Ritual of Coffin Making in a City Hit by Ebola
items.summary: While several coffin makers in Bunia said they were providing a public service, the virus has put them at the center of a debate around safe burials.

items.title: Can Ancient Ruins Be Protected From Wildfires? Greece Is Trying.
items.summary: As blazes surge across Europe, the country is making a trade-off to protect its heritage by fireproofing sites at the risk of spoiling the surrounding landscape.

items.title: A Factory in Rural Ireland Is at the Center of a Dispute Over Russia
items.summary: Alumina processed at a refinery in County Limerick may be feeding Russia’s war in Ukraine, an investigation suggested. There is little agreement on what to do about it.

items.title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln to Dock in Thailand on Wednesday, Pattaya Mayor Says
items.summary: The U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln became an emblem of the strains of the war on the U.S. military. Now its crew will have some rest.

items.title: U.S. Sanctions on Iran Cut Off Students from Tests Needed for Study Abroad
items.summary: The latest measures have forced the cancellation of English proficiency and graduate exams, isolating many Iranians most eager to foster ties with the world.

items.title: These Generals Fought for Israel. Now They See ‘Jewish Terrorism’ as the Threat.
items.summary: A growing number of former Israeli generals, intelligence officials and prime ministers are accusing settlers in the West Bank of committing ethnic cleansing with government support. “Once a society behaves this way,” one said, “that society is doomed.”

items.title: For Nepal’s Young Leader, Flood Recovery Will Be a Herculean Task
items.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah, 36, rose to power this year on the back of youth anger with graft and mismanagement. His fledgling government now faces a huge test.

items.title: Nonstop Russian Drones Make for Dangerous New Phase of War in Kyiv
items.summary: The nearly constant air raids, a shift from years of largely overnight attacks, have left residents exhausted and on edge.

items.title: ‘The Nest of Snakes’: Warring Cartels Target Women in Mexico
items.summary: A two-year war between rival Sinaloa Cartel factions is driving a surge in killings and disappearances targeting women.

items.title: How the Pentagon Is Getting Into the Venezuelan Oil Business Under Trump
items.summary: The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, founded by the Biden administration to give loans to bolster the U.S. defense industry, is helping lead President Trump’s oil deal.

items.title: Shein’s Lackluster Debut Shows a Fast-Fashion Model Left Behind
items.summary: Squeezed by new trade rules, shrinking market share and labor concerns, Shein’s share decline in Hong Kong on Tuesday is a sign investors have moved on.

items.title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Firm Leads $1 Billion Funding Round for Polymarket
items.summary: The new round values the prediction market at $21 billion, up from $15 billion. Mr. Trump’s firm, 1789 Capital, will invest around $300 million.

items.title: Expedia Fights Off Claim for Damages by Cuban Exile Families
items.summary: A jury in Florida found that in their suit against the travel booking company, the plaintiffs had failed to prove ownership over tourism properties in Cuba.

items.title: IRS Audit Revenue Has Plummeted Under Trump, Watchdog Finds
items.summary: The I.R.S. lost roughly a quarter of its employees since President Trump took office, hampering the agency’s ability to conduct audits.

items.title: Kalshi Permanently Bars George Santos From the Platform
items.summary: The prediction market said it had barred George Santos, the former congressman from New York, and fined him $71,356 over evidence he engaged in insider trading.

items.title: Private Equity Wants to Invest in College Sports. Some Schools Are Wary.
items.summary: As desperate as many athletic programs are for money, they are proceeding cautiously when it comes to deals with private equity.

items.title: U.S. Start-Up and Saudi Arabia Form Data Center Partnership
items.summary: Together AI, which serves open-source artificial intelligence models, announced a deal to use compute from Humain in Saudi Arabia, where it can bypass U.S. backlash over data centers.

items.title: Global Oil Price Rises to $90 a Barrel After U.S. and Iran Trade Attacks
items.summary: The first attacks in a month jolted energy markets. The average U.S. gasoline price remained 37 percent higher since the war began.

items.title: Europe Protests as U.S. Invites Russian Minister to G20 Finance Meeting
items.summary: The meeting, which China and Russia are attending, is focused on the ongoing economic shock from the war in Iran, which has driven up oil prices globally.

items.title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
items.summary: Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced more than a million advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.

items.title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
items.summary: State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.

items.title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
items.summary: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.

items.title: Prediction Markets and States Clashed, Setting Off a Furious Political Battle
items.summary: A legal dispute over the future of Kalshi, Polymarket and others has drawn in the Trump administration, the president’s son and nearly every state attorney general.

items.title: John Ternus Replaces Tim Cook as Apple CEO
items.summary: Big technology and management changes are greeting John Ternus, whose long-serving predecessor, Tim Cook, will stay on as executive chair.

items.title: Influencers Have a Lot to Say About Politics. Many Are Quietly Paid for It.
items.summary: Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.

items.title: Prediction Markets Should Be Regulated as Gambling, Appeals Court Says
items.summary: The outcome contradicted an earlier appeals court decision. Federal regulators said the split rulings called for resolution by the Supreme Court.

items.title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
items.summary: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.

items.title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
items.summary: Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.

items.title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
items.summary: The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.
